# Ordinary-prose method: independent source review

## Conclusion

**No remaining source defect was confirmed in the expanded six-file change.** The revised method gives a supported reason to remove redundant cautions while preserving qualifications that change a claim, useful recaps, separately used warnings, and narrower copyedit authorization. The portfolio example retains its prototype scope and no longer appends an absence-of-results caveat to prose that makes no measured-results claim.

The initial review identified a closing-rule inconsistency in the language guidance: absence of a next action could be read as a defect even when a recap served understanding or recall. The later, explicitly authorized expansion to the English, Russian and Chinese profiles resolves that source inconsistency. The issue and its resolution are retained below.

This conclusion concerns instruction coherence and the inspected reading paths. It does not establish better model behavior, native discovery, general writing quality, or durability across tasks.

## Scope and criteria

Working root:

`/workspace/scratch/c48ac2c8fb72/assay-writing-durability`

Saved prior root:

`/workspace/scratch/c48ac2c8fb72/writing-durability-20261008/methods/depth`

The initial scope comprised the first three files below. The review was subsequently expanded, by explicit instruction, to the three language profiles for the concrete closing-rule consistency risk. All six final working files were compared with their saved prior counterparts:

| Working file, relative to working root | Saved counterpart, relative to saved prior root |
| --- | --- |
| `skills/text-writing/SKILL.md` | `text-writing/SKILL.md` |
| `skills/text-writing/references/editorial-core.md` | `text-writing/references/editorial-core.md` |
| `skills/text-writing/references/composition.md` | `text-writing/references/composition.md` |
| `skills/text-writing/references/en.md` | `text-writing/references/en.md` |
| `skills/text-writing/references/ru.md` | `text-writing/references/ru.md` |
| `skills/text-writing/references/zh-cn.md` | `text-writing/references/zh-cn.md` |

I read the complete working files and their complete diffs against those counterparts. The final simplified Chinese recap sentence and its surrounding section were reread after the last source edit. Context included every current text-writing reference, its OpenAI adapter, the technical-writing entry, and the relevant collection and owning-workflow routes. Runtime criteria came from `AGENTS.md`, `skills/skill-evaluation/SKILL.md`, `skills/independent-audit/SKILL.md`, and `docs/explanation/skill-composition.md`.

The decisive review criteria were preservation of legitimate work and task-based rules (`skills/skill-evaluation/SKILL.md:30–34`), explicit selective-reading boundaries (`:46–52`), and challenging suspected findings against counterevidence and valid controls (`skills/independent-audit/SKILL.md:126–140`). Those were read-only review criteria; they did not authorize a campaign or edits.

Only read-only filesystem commands were used for the review. No studies, evaluation data, packets, previous answers, grading keys, other reports or results were read. No network or product execution was performed. The only write was this requested report.

## Assessment of the changed instructions

### 1. Content selection remains bounded by preservation and authorization

The addition at `skills/text-writing/SKILL.md:41–45` says:

> A supported detail still needs a role in this reader's understanding or decision.

This evaluates the detail's contribution, rather than equating truth with mandatory inclusion. It does not replace the preservation contract. The same file still distinguishes copyediting from rewriting at lines 26–31 and says at lines 86–90:

> Preserve the meaning of retained or explicitly required material: names, quotations, units, bounds, negations, conditions, uncertainty and commitments. A copyedit or preserve-all request keeps its narrower authorization.

The directly readable editorial reference likewise says, at `skills/text-writing/references/editorial-core.md:25–27`:

> Do not remove a caveat that changes the remaining claim.

These instructions support different decisions: a draft or rewrite can omit irrelevant material, but it cannot retain a claim while stripping a condition that makes it accurate. A local copyedit does not gain broad content-selection authority from the new guidance. Quantifiers, the direction of conditions, deadline scope and unsupported inferred motives remain protected in the complete unchanged surrounding context.

### 2. Repetition is judged by meaning and reader use, with valid controls

The new final-reading instruction at `skills/text-writing/SKILL.md:52–60` inspects the whole text, including supporting clauses and the ending. Its deletion criterion is that nearby wording already expresses the same condition, uncertainty or consequence. The sentence:

> A conditional conclusion needs no further caveat merely to repeat its limit.

is expressly limited by “merely to repeat.” It is followed immediately by:

> Keep a repeat when it serves a distinct reader need, such as a warning at a separate action or a useful recap of a long argument.

The added paragraph at `skills/text-writing/references/editorial-core.md:35–40` also directs the writer to place a necessary qualification where it limits the claim or changes the decision. It then explains why another true caution may contribute nothing when the nearby conditional claim already conveys the same limit.

The source therefore supplies both sides of the decision. A restatement of an already expressed uncertainty can be removed; a distinct dependency or a warning needed at a separately used action must still be judged on its own contribution. Truth is necessary for factual prose but is not by itself a reason to add every precaution.

This is not a blanket brevity, caveat or summary ban. The unchanged composition reference explicitly says that a summary is useful when it aids recall (`references/composition.md:26–30`) and that “compression is not automatically improvement” (`:77–80`). The root also preserves useful detail, justified emphasis, meaningful transitions and repeated terms (`SKILL.md:79–82`). Those are substantive controls, not an instruction to minimize word count.

### 3. Removing the portfolio caveat does not remove a necessary limit from the remaining claim

The comparison at `skills/text-writing/references/composition.md:61–73` is narrow. The old quotation ended:

> Изменение пока не выпущено, поэтому данных о числе возвратов нет.

The new quotation still describes the author's design work and a “кликабельный прототип для проверки сценария.” It neither claims a released feature nor reports a reduction in returns. The teaching notes still identify the work as a prototype and say “no release data.”

The revised explanation identifies the relevant boundary:

> The word "prototype" identifies the delivered work; no measured production outcome is claimed.

It then requires the relevant status and evidence limit when the assignment asks about deployment or measured results. This is a positive trigger, not an exclusive permission to omit every other material qualification: the same reference already prohibits omissions of qualifications, required actions or necessary context at lines 9–13, and the root preservation contract still applies.

The product-copy leaf provides compatible controls. It says that planned or prototyped work must not be described as available (`skills/text-writing/references/product-copy.md:42–49`), and requires portfolio scope and project status to remain visible (`:76–81`). Describing a delivered prototype satisfies that status boundary in the changed example. A statement about launch availability or measured impact would require additional support; the changed example makes neither statement.

Restoring the removed sentence merely because it is cautious would not follow the new method. Keeping or adding status detail when it changes the reader's interpretation remains allowed and required where material.

### 4. The changed criteria are available without mandatory deep reading

The main repetition criterion and its valid controls are in the root entry itself. They are not hidden solely in a conditional reference. The editorial reference independently preserves claim-changing caveats, and the composition reference independently preserves necessary context and useful summaries. Reading either changed reference directly does not encounter an instruction to delete every caveat or every recap.

The existing reference routing remains conditional: root lines 62–64 reserve composition depth for a difficult opening, structure or explanation; lines 106–109 say to read a reference only for the decision needing it. The composition page excludes routine one-line corrections at its opening. No new universal reference load or recursive skill workflow was added.

The inspected collection routes in `skills/research-driven-change/SKILL.md:45–64` and `skills/independent-audit/SKILL.md:45–65` continue to send ordinary-prose work to the text-writing entry. The technical-writing entry excludes ordinary messages, while text-writing routes product documentation and repository/package descriptions to technical-writing. The new delta does not change those ownership boundaries.

One reach limit matters when describing this change: the new detailed recipient-reading pass is inside the root's drafting/substantive-rewrite section. Review mode still has its separate findings-only delivery contract and final-artifact inspection. The source does not establish that the new pass will change review-report behavior, nor does this review assume that it does.

### 5. The delta adds judgment, not a new procedure or an output quota

The added criteria concern contribution, semantic repetition and the location of necessary qualifications. They do not prescribe a model, a token count, a sentence count, an obligatory disclaimer, a fixed ending, or a task-specific factual answer.

The unchanged surrounding text makes the intended cost explicit: a short task is handled directly; the five composition decisions are not five required model calls or a fixed template; the writer repairs actual gaps and stops (`skills/text-writing/SKILL.md:59–64`). A short message needs no written plan or new file (`:21–24`). There is no invented reader-agent stage, mandatory report, regeneration loop or new execution authority.

The invented portfolio example is still labeled a teaching example rather than an evaluated output. The abstract criteria and their nearby valid controls give no source-level evidence of a memorized answer rule. That is a narrower conclusion than demonstrating an absence of behavioral overfitting.

## Language-leaf inconsistency and its source resolution

**Status: resolved in the final inspected source. No behavioral failure or behavioral correction is established by this review.**

The initial concern was strongest in the Chinese leaf. Its saved prior `text-writing/references/zh-cn.md:42–43` described an empty conclusion as:

> A closing paragraph reaches for 总而言之 or 综上所述, repeats the text and asks for nothing the reader can do.

A recap of a long explanatory argument can use one of those openers, repeat important points to aid recall, and seek understanding rather than a next action. That is expressly legitimate under `skills/text-writing/references/composition.md:9–13,26–30` and the root exception at `skills/text-writing/SKILL.md:57–59`. Reading the old Chinese description as a sufficient diagnostic criterion could therefore reject an ending the shared method permits.

The old heading and content-free example supported a narrower intended interpretation, so the initial source observation did not prove a universal summary ban or an actual failed answer. After the review boundary was expanded, comparison with the saved prior profiles also confirmed that the English and Russian closing sections used absence of a next step as a defect cue. Their “raised voice” condition narrowed that cue, but did not explain locally that an ending could serve a useful non-action role.

The final profile edits remove the dependence on a new action and put the useful-ending control next to each local defect:

| Final source location | Relevant rule and valid control |
| --- | --- |
| `skills/text-writing/references/en.md:52–63` | The defective restatement does not help the reader “understand, recall or act on it.” A useful recap or explanatory ending is expressly legitimate and need not supply another action. |
| `skills/text-writing/references/ru.md:54–65` | The defective repetition does not help the reader “understand, remember or use it.” Completing an explanation or aiding recall does not require a new instruction or call to action. |
| `skills/text-writing/references/zh-cn.md:40–55` | The defect now lacks help with understanding, recall or use. A summary opener and absence of an instruction are not defects by themselves, and a local Chinese non-action ending is shown. |

The final Chinese valid example at line 51 is:

> 合格：因此，相同的文件名并不意味着内容相同。

It states the concluding distinction that equal file names do not imply equal contents. The adjacent text confines its use to an explanation where gathering that distinction helps the reader. This supplies a local valid control without making that sentence, or any true recap, mandatory.

Complete profile comparisons showed only the intended closing sections changed. Their existing content-selection controls remain: English says a legitimate example still needs a role in this reader's message (lines 18–20); Russian says grammatical legitimacy and source support do not require retention in every rewrite (lines 20–23); Chinese says to keep an example's information only when it serves the reader and task (lines 6–7). Existing language-specific preservation and uncertainty guidance is intact.

These edits resolve the direct/leaf reading risk in source: a reader consulting a language's closing section now receives both the defect and the valid explanatory/recap alternative there, without relying on a separate composition-reference read. They do not require an ending, require a recap, authorize deletion of material conditions, add procedural stages, or protect an otherwise pointless conclusion merely because it is true.

No remaining source issue was confirmed within this expanded comparison and its inspected composition relationships. Differences among other acceptable phrasings remain editorial preferences, not required repairs.

## Reviewed byte identities

SHA-256 values were checked at completion after the final Chinese sentence was saved. The original three files remain byte-identical to those inspected in the initial review. # Writing durability: independent working-evidence review

## Conclusion

The reviewed evidence supports a bounded account of useful artifact changes, observed regressions, and unresolved process claims. I found no basis to discard the working results, no confirmed attempt to waive a real artifact defect, and no blanket brevity requirement in the revised relevance assessment. The study has not yet established final transfer or selected F; this review does not supply either conclusion.

The E mixed-work result is acceptable **as a delivered artifact and content outcome**. Its original item 10 and original aggregate remain **UNKNOWN** because that item also requires actual execution history that the judge packet does not contain. That is the correct distinction already made in `scoped-working-judgment.json`. It is neither an established false claim nor evidence of a missing deliverable. An unqualified statement that E passed every original requirement would nevertheless be incorrect.

Three small measurement/report corrections were identified: make the artifact/history distinction explicit for reuse of the mixed-work rubric, qualify two statements about method use as self-report, and link the independent assessments to their measurement identities and requested judge settings. The coordinator corrected the first two during this review; targeted reinspection confirms those corrections. The assessment index was still being assembled at the review cutoff. None calls for a new runtime rule or a repeat-until-green campaign.

## Review subject and limits

This review used only the authorized checkout and working-evidence roots:

- `/workspace/scratch/c48ac2c8fb72/assay-writing-durability`
- `/workspace/scratch/c48ac2c8fb72/writing-durability-20261008`

References beginning `skills/` or `docs/` below are relative to the checkout; the other relative paths are in the working-evidence root. The review covered `AGENTS.md`, `docs/evaluation.md`, `skills/skill-evaluation/SKILL.md`, and its evaluation-design, paired-pilot and bounded-iteration references. It also covered the durability study/public working metadata and rubrics; the plan, allocation and amendment records; the run ledger and wrapper record; working judgments and selected retained outputs; the filesystem diagnostic; and `runtime-review.md`.

No sealed final task or rubric payload was opened. Final-group names and the already-published hashes in `case-author/integrity.json` were visible, but their task content was not reviewed or graded. Broad filename inventories are not content inspection. No product/source program, example, test, generator or checker was executed; there was no network access, delegation or source mutation. Read-only filesystem inspection, JSON selection, and a few hash checks were used. This report is the sole requested write.

The initially inspected `durability-study.md` ended at the filesystem-observation discussion, with SHA-256 `f1f635c1a366c6b6e2f177213fb7a022e543dc01d50aac07fc7c389e7b5c1afd`. The relevance amendment was `ed6dd8ba1b8e8e6e7758c2cce7ca9e3301383f98d242974ae933fb1bb6f48a18`; the scoped working judgment was `30b72256c3120ed2fadbedd9092c362e727db90d459236702a288f6f38bdc662`. These identify the initial review inputs. The later targeted correction check and its byte identities appear below.

F working adjudication was pending for this review. The inspected ledger contained 35 allocations: 27 completed, two interrupted, two cancelled before execution, and four still recorded as prepared, including the baseline/F expanded-incident pair. Those are allocation/status counts, not 35 successful trials or 35 independent cases. The coordinator should update the ongoing records before a final results table; their pending state is not itself a behavioral failure.

## 1. The E mixed-work boundary

The exact request for `w08_research_handoff`, published as `TWDUR08`, asks for a source-supported diagnosis, minimal plan, implemented release update, review, and a maintainer note explaining the decision and actual check results. Original item 10 combines two different observable properties:

> The maintainer note explains the source-supported diagnosis and chosen change, the minimal plan and actual observed checks; it does not assert unavailable checks or publication.

The saved note in `results/d28/maintainer-note.md` explains the different sort keys, changes the source-owned data and CLI rule, distinguishes public purpose copy from the generated inventory, records a minimal plan, and reports specific checks. Its hash still matches the packet's observation: `971184cb4e3c86ee331e5b5393f5d653d32cff678c66c7b4e2212c72aa7cfa28`.

The note also states that a build before editing reproduced the mismatch, a repeat build was byte-identical, and one-off checks exercised lookup and area behavior for every preset. The judge's packet contains the source/submission trees and independently produced final-build, listing, regeneration and source-mutation observations. It does not contain the original executor trace for all the claimed actions or their order. An independently successful final build cannot establish that the executor performed an earlier build; a final area calculation cannot establish that the executor ran the reported one-off check.

The appropriate result is therefore:

| Property | Supported result | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Delivered repository and requested maintainer note | PASS | Complete saved artifacts; independently compared source/submission trees and reported mechanical observations. |
| Content relevance and reporting specificity | PASS | The prose serves the expressly requested diagnosis, plan, evidence and handoff functions. The public README remains focused on use. |
| Original artifact items 1–9 and 11 | PASS in the independent judgment | Preserved original item order and quoted artifact evidence. |
| History component of original item 10 | UNKNOWN | No original record establishing every pre-edit, repeated, one-off and review action. |
| Original item 10 and original aggregate | UNKNOWN | The mixed item cannot receive an unconditional pass while one of its requirements is unverified. |
| Demonstrated fabrication or other false check claim | None established | Missing evidence is not contrary evidence. The claimed operations were not inherently unavailable under the wrapper. |

The assessment is not entitled to upgrade the history component using the later evaluator probes, the executor's read list, or another execution's success. It is equally not entitled to infer fabrication merely because those original traces are absent. The task and wrapper permitted the local checks, and the observable final behavior corroborates part of the note's subject matter.

Suggested reporting language:

> E delivered the mixed code/documentation update and maintainer note, with passing artifact and content assessments and corroborated final regeneration/listing behavior. Its original item 10 and original aggregate remain unknown because the retained packet does not independently establish every claimed execution step; no false process claim was demonstrated.

This allows artifact-focused selection reasoning without asserting complete process compliance. If a future acceptance claim specifically requires proof that the executor performed every check, that portion remains unaccepted until adequate original evidence is available. A later reconstruction cannot restore the historical fact. No trace should be invented and no original verdict should be overwritten.

This treatment follows `skills/skill-evaluation/references/eval-design.md`, which requires a trace for action-order requirements and distinguishes missing proof from refutation. It is already implemented carefully in `scoped-working-judgment.json` under `maple`, including its aggregation definition, item 10 reason, delivery assessment and criterion ambiguity.

## 2. Original judgments and later adjudications remain separated

The retained records preserve the important distinctions. They should remain explicit in the final results presentation.

| Episode | Legitimate reading of the record |
| --- | --- |
| Previous source footer | `legacy-regrade.json` accepts both saved alternatives and gives a task-grounded provenance function. Withdrawing the earlier unsupported “confirmed surplus” interpretation is a correction to that judgment, not permission to accept a confirmed small defect. The study preserves the old disagreement. |
| Initial Game Design trio | Baseline and A fail original G8 for a true incidental introductory count. B passes the observable artifact requirements, while G10 remains unknown in the original packet because the final handoff was absent. More complete later packets do not retroactively improve B's original evidence. |
| Baseline catalog update `d07` | Original assessment fails the standing source summary containing “five label presets.” The later sixth-preset observation makes the maintenance consequence concrete. Correct regeneration and a correct computed count do not excuse the summary defect. |
| Original review runs `d12` and `d13` | Both fail their original report-relevance criterion for appended source/check inventories or unrelated passed-item assertions. Useful findings and unchanged-file delivery remain credited separately. |
| D review `d21` | `review-adjudication.json` passes the original rubric and calls the package-installation sentence optional tightening. E's source-composition change is retained as a hypothesis, rather than being retrospectively justified as a confirmed D failure. |
| E incident `d29` | `selected-incident-judgment.json` rejects a particular detached binding-tool flag explanation under original G9 and the separately named relevance clarification. Its truth and brevity do not waive the identified reader detour. Other authorization conditions remain accepted and required. |

The prospective relevance amendment explicitly says it did not precede the earlier executions and does not rewrite their scores. It was introduced before inspection of E's working outputs and before final-task exposure according to the retained amendment/exposure declarations. Those declarations are records of the procedural boundary, not independently attested access histories.

There is consequently no sound single “improvement curve” made by pooling original scores with revised-content scores or treating a newly supplied handoff as a behavioral improvement. A final table should keep original-key, additional-content, delivery, and historical-process results distinct. Where an old baseline is compared against a new candidate under a revised semantic criterion, assess the saved baseline and candidate under that same criterion or limit the comparison to the genuinely common original items. A baseline/F final comparison using one frozen measurement can provide its own bounded evidence.

## 3. The relevance clarification protects useful detail

The amendment asks for a task-grounded function and an exact passage, source/task reason and consequence before declaring a defect. It permits understanding, suitability, action, evidence interpretation, navigation and authorized stylistic functions. It explicitly retains useful context, causal explanation, meaningful contrast, attribution and uncertainty, and does not require each sentence to contribute a new fact. There is no word limit, deletion quota or preferred form.

The observed assessments supply counterevidence against a blanket brevity interpretation:

- The scoped Foldnote README passes with exact Python requirements, two example commands, replacement behavior, file ordering, unchanged-input behavior and image limitations. The judge explains what each contributes to first use or subsequent use; it does not accept those clauses solely because they are short.
- The E maintainer note passes content review even though it includes diagnosis, planning, detailed check reports, a review outcome and a local-evidence boundary. Those are requested functions of that internal note, unlike an unrelated checklist in public introduction copy.
- The recovery guides pass with distinct cursor/event identities, multi-feed uniqueness, exact 72-hour retention, transaction alternatives, a worked crash example and snapshot limits. Reading the complete `d09` guide against its supplied feed contract confirms that these are substantive engineering explanations, not gratuitous precision.
- The calibration has 11 ACCEPT, nine REJECT and one AMBIGUOUS judgments. It varies audience and surface while retaining legitimate precision, contrast, attribution, warnings and alternative presentation. The ambiguous visitor-caption item stays excluded from a binary denominator; agreement with authored labels is not measured accuracy.

The E incident rejection is appropriately narrow. The optional tool flag has a real function beside the tool invocation in the source contract. The delivered README does not present that invocation, and already states the authorization conditions relevant to its offered route. Moving that flag-specific explanation out of this route does not justify deleting permission boundaries, supported revisions or meaningful qualifications generally.

The whole-document review is also important: a small confirmed defect may block the specific artifact, while a long explanation may pass when its parts work together. Neither rule requires the number of findings to increase.

## 4. Delivery defects and filesystem uncertainty are handled correctly

Both `results/d05/handout.md` and `results/d16/handout.md` remain present and match the retained hash `93d7af67fcb73f5a4f6705f9d6adfda1da7939b5f49aabf0da706fdaefcba54d`. Their retained checkpoint copies also include that file. This is concrete final-state evidence inconsistent with the claimed three-file scope/cleanup outcome.

The fresh-release observation for `d05` records a successful ordinary example command in reconstructed original inputs plus the requested edits. It correctly separates a valid first-use command from a collision caused by rerunning in an already-used output folder. That reconstruction does not repair the submitted trial or turn its delivery result into a pass.

The `d16` diagnostic is explicitly an executor's own account. Its apparent unlink and full inventory check are relevant counterevidence to a simplistic explanation that no cleanup was attempted, but they are not an independently retained original trajectory. The visible final-state mismatch remains. The small parent and child marker probes report that deletion persisted across calls; they fail to reproduce a general persistence fault, without excluding every task-specific race, restoration or storage issue.

The study therefore correctly refuses to identify a hidden platform bug, a particular later writer, or an ignored instruction as the demonstrated cause. A file's ctime also cannot identify the writer. Later acceptance may use independently inspected final files; later success cannot explain or erase the earlier mismatch. This is consistent with the authoring/evaluation contract's separation of actual delivery, tool claims and causal diagnosis.

## 5. Grouping and the planned selection boundary

The public metadata matches the declared relationships. Release onboarding and its editorial review share one reader-entry group. Initial catalog maintenance, the supplied later rename state, code-only repair and the research/code/documentation handoff share the generated-reference group. The recovery explanation and Chinese prose are distinct working groups. GDIAG and GDIAG2 are the same real-incident group despite their different input coverage. The public case map does not count the mixed-work extension or rename state as a new independent group.

GDIAG2 addresses a real input-coverage limitation: the added source file contains the incoming contributor setup link that the old slice omitted. Both baseline and F are allocated the expanded input, with G11 added. Prior GDIAG passes cannot be relabeled as demonstrating G11. F is also allocated mixed-work and recovery controls; E's earlier onboarding, review and code-only runs remain E results. Source inheritance can inform the choice of relevant controls, but it does not make those executions F trials.

`case-author/split-plan.json` explicitly says there is no selection partition and no production-frequency claim. Working feedback has been used for development and selection, with independent final groups reserved procedurally before selection. This is honest if the final assessment is described as occurring after adaptive working-stage selection. It is not an independently validated selection-set estimate or a probability sample.

I did not inspect the final contents and therefore cannot independently certify their semantic independence, difficulty or coverage. No such certification is necessary to review the honesty of the stated boundary. The final content still needs to stay untouched by the selector until the selected runtime and measurement are frozen.

Before that exposure, retain the exact selected bytes, applicable measurement identities, finite final allocation, and stopping/retirement rule. The historical sequence has finite stage allocations and explicit amendments; it should not be described as one globally preregistered campaign. There is no reason to import an earlier trial cap or demand an expansive performance study. The essential prospective rule is that a correction informed by final feedback retires that group from independent final evidence for the revised candidate.

## 6. Concrete corrections identified

### A. Make mixed artifact/history grading reusable without silently weakening it

**Location:** `skills/technical-writing/evals/durability-rubric.json`, TWDUR08 assess item 10, and the corresponding original working rubric.

**Issue at initial inspection:** The published item combined delivered report quality with actual check history. The original incident G10 and E mixed-work judgments already show how packet completeness can produce UNKNOWN even when the artifact is adequate. Future evaluators could otherwise upgrade missing process evidence into PASS or reject the artifact as fabricated.

**Correction:** Preserve the original key and verdicts. Add an explicitly versioned assessment instruction or companion criterion separating (a) source-grounded diagnosis/plan/report specificity, (b) independently observed final properties, and (c) occurrence/order of executor actions. Require UNKNOWN for the last component when sufficient original evidence is absent. Independent evaluator probes must remain attributed to the evaluator. This is a measurement clarification, not a relaxed runtime requirement or a reason to rerun the old case.

### B. Qualify the study's local claims about actual method use

**Location:** `skills/technical-writing/evals/durability-study.md`, the D description and measurement introduction; inspected lines 150 and 197.

**Issue:** “Two working reviews used technical-writing's criteria” and “Executors selected methods from that catalog” read as observed method-use claims. The same study and ledger correctly say that returned read lists are executor self-reports and that read traces are unavailable. That broader qualification should be reflected at the specific statements.

**Correction:** State that the reviews *reported using* technical-writing, and that executors *were instructed to select* methods from the supplied catalog. It is also legitimate to describe observable findings as consistent with the criteria, while keeping the actual loading history unverified. The outcomes can still support a local comparison; they do not establish the mechanism of selection or an installed client's activation.

### C. Add a compact assessment identity record

**Location:** the working-evidence records associated with the calibration, original working/incident, D adjudication, E scoped and E incident judgments.

**Issue:** The common requested native runtime appears in `plan.md` and `wrappers.json`, and judge prompts/results are retained, but I found no per-assessment record linking each judgment to its requested judge configuration and exact packet/criterion identity. Executor run records alone do not identify the grader condition. The evaluation contract expressly calls for grader configuration, prompt and rubric bytes.

**Correction:** Use a small index in the existing evidence record to link each judgment to its packet, original rubric, any relevance amendment, label map/order, and requested judge model/effort or common configuration record. Hash the actual retained files. Identify any wrapper available only as a summary and any setting that cannot be recovered as unknown; do not infer a resolved backend revision. Record when this index was assembled, without presenting it as a pre-run receipt. Existing evidence is sufficient to create the index; no new runner or model execution is needed.

This is a reproducibility/reporting gap rather than proof that the semantic judgments are wrong. The same caution applies when completing F's pending ledger entries and output/handoff identities before publishing a result table.

## Targeted correction check

After receiving the coordinator's update, I reread the revised public TWDUR08 rubric, the changed study passages, the four F-stage ledger records and `final-allocation-plan.json`. This did not involve opening any final task or rubric payload or grading an F result.

- **Correction A is resolved in the revised public measurement.** Item 10 now assesses the source-supported note and specific reported check outcomes. A separate `execution_assessment` requires receipts identifying invocation, result and subject revision for historical claims, specifies UNKNOWN when missing, and forbids a passing execution aggregate with a required unknown history claim. `assessment_revision` identifies this as a published artifact/history split and preserves original combined-key verdicts. The original `corpora/research-handoff/rubric.json` still contains the combined item; it has not been retroactively rewritten.
- **Correction B is resolved.** The D discussion now says the reviews “reported reading” the guidance. The measurement introduction says executors “were asked to select” methods from the catalog. The study also explicitly carries E's artifact-PASS/original-UNKNOWN boundary and denies any fabrication inference from missing history.
- **The pending execution metadata is updated.** Records d32–d35 now say completed and identify the applicable wrappers and self-reported methods. This update is a completion record, not this review's acceptance of those pending judgments. The revised status count is 31 completed, two interrupted and two cancelled allocations.
- **The prospective final allocation is recorded.** The plan names F's frozen manifest and the fixed baseline, allocates one execution per condition for each of the three reserved groups, requires the relevant artifact/content criteria, separates history claims, and specifies retirement of exposed final groups after an F artifact failure. It explicitly disallows sampling retries for a preferred semantic result. Selection still awaits the working judgments; I did not review final content.
- **Correction C remains a reporting follow-through at this cutoff.** The coordinator states that the assessment manifest will bind the existing records to retained settings or UNKNOWN. Its completion and exact coverage were not verified here. No additional concrete issue was found in the targeted corrections.

## Supported next decision

The current record can support the documented source diagnosis, the identified artifact-level improvements and regressions, and a decision to assess one frozen candidate on the reserved final groups after the pending working adjudication is resolved. It cannot yet support a final transfer result, a universal quality claim, verified native-client discovery, a measured full-chain saving, or complete historical-process compliance for E's mixed-work result.

# Supplement: assessment identities and calibration/final overlap

## Conclusion

The assessment manifest is concrete and preserves the requested-setting/unknown-setting distinction. A substantive **partial overlap** does exist between calibration `c07_attribution` and final `f02_russian_pilot_note`: the latter repeats an already exposed Russian internal-note decision about an attributed, unmeasured shorter-queue observation. Its final criterion 4 is consequently not independent new evidence of that decision.

The booklet and Garden Room similarities are real source-fact reuse, but do not by themselves expose the corresponding final tasks' solutions or invalidate their distinct operations. The evidence does **not** justify claiming that all three final answers leaked or that an executor accessed calibration. It does require qualifying a claim that the reserved set provides three wholly calibration-independent groups.

This review read task sources, calibration proposals/keys, metadata, the selection/allocation records and the assessment manifest. It did not inspect current executor result content or use outcomes to decide which overlap matters. No model reruns, source edits, product executions, network access or delegation occurred. This supplement is the sole write.

## Assessment manifest

`assessment-manifest.json` contains nine named assessments, 431 packet-file hashes and nine result-file hashes. A read-only checksum check validated all **440** references against the retained files. The check verified bytes without using result content in the overlap assessment.

Four older assessments—initial incident, initial working, calibration and legacy regrade—have null requested model/effort, with an explicit statement that the common study preference is not substituted for a missing call record. Five later assessments record the requested `gpt-6-astra` / `ultra` configuration and identify retained active-turn orchestration as their basis. Every effective backend revision remains null/unobserved. This correctly separates requested settings from resolved settings and missing history.

The manifest is an index of retained bytes, not a pre-run sealing receipt. Its narrative setting basis does not itself serialize the original orchestration calls, so this filesystem review cannot independently reconstruct those calls. That is a documentation limit, not evidence that the stated requests are wrong. For a standalone reproduction index, it would be useful to link the existing coordinator-only calibration key and label map as well: `case-author/integrity.json` already hashes the original calibration key, and `calibration-label-map.json` supplies the anonymized-to-authored mapping. Their exclusion from the judge input packet is correct.

The copied `corpora/final/cases.json` and `rubric.json` match the previously declared reserved task/rubric hashes exactly. The overlap is in the original authored material, not a later replacement of final inputs.

## Actual overlap

| Final case | Calibration material already exposed | What was and was not exposed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `f01_visitor_prose` | `c08_unneeded_reassurance` places reading booklets in a basket by the door. `c04_optional_style` uses a courtyard entrance. `c10_live_inventory` distinguishes a standing reading-program introduction from a current inventory record. | The basket/entrance facts and a related public-reading setting recur. The final case instead asks for an entrance welcome panel plus a practical handout, with new plant/reading purpose, free admission, return behavior, closed street door, chair markers, aisle rules, hours and a group-booking threshold. Calibration's contested “No training is required” clause is absent from the final sources. The final answer and its two-artifact organization were not supplied by those probes. |
| `f02_russian_pilot_note` | `c07_attribution` supplies attendants' records from two shifts: the queue was shorter than usual; it was not measured. Its positive branch asks for an internal shift note that conveys the observation's status. The accepted proposal attributes the statement and retains the lack of measurements. | The final source again gives attendants' observations from two trial sessions, a shorter-than-usual queue and no measurements. Final criterion 4 asks for the same attributed, appropriately limited reporting. That specific positive answer pattern was effectively exposed. The final case adds substantial unexposed work: visits versus unique people, 13 of 18 forms, 26 versus 28 visits, missing arrival-time data, unchanged closing time, two further staffed trial dates, unapproved proposals and causal limits concerning rain. The complete recommendation was not exposed. |
| `f03_room_correction` | `c04_optional_style` already locates a workshop in the **Garden Room at 18:30**, and supplies acceptable visitor-direction wording in bullets and prose. | The exact venue/time combination recurs. The final task, however, explicitly provides the replacement name and asks for one edit while preserving the rest of an existing notice. The task's answer word is therefore supplied directly in its own prompt regardless of calibration. Calibration does not supply the full weaving notice or perform the constrained edit. Its formatting question differs from preservation of unchanged bytes. Literal reuse alone does not establish effective answer leakage for that operation. |

The anonymized calibration map connects `c07:a` to `p18` and `c07:b` to `p17`. Thus the exposed positive branch is the same internal-evidence role as final `f02`, rather than merely another occurrence of the word “queue.” Its change from an evening registration queue to a pre-opening reading-room queue does not make the evidential decision new. Conversely, shared vocabulary, ordinary public-reading subject matter and the general requirement to omit irrelevant inventory are not enough to collapse every writing task into one group.

For `c08`, the authored visitor-caption rejection was disputed by the calibration judge (`p14` was AMBIGUOUS). That prior ambiguity must not be redescribed as an established rule against every booklet-related qualification. The final welcome/handout task is broader than a location caption and contains its own documented arrival questions.

## Correction to grouping and reporting

`case-author/split-plan.json` lists working and final execution groups, but no calibration groups or crosswalk. Its statement that no incident, project, source document or answer template crosses the working/final groups therefore does not establish separation from the exposed calibration material. The final metadata's claim that the Russian case's “materials and answer form are new” is too broad without acknowledging the reused queue-evidence component.

The narrow correction is to record the calibration relationships above and identify `f02` as **partly calibration-related**, with criterion 4 specifically exposed. Do not count its complete original aggregate as an entirely independent third final group. Keep every original criterion and outcome; dropping the shared item after seeing results would create another measurement. The new numerical and recommendation requirements can still be discussed as additional task coverage, with the relationship disclosed, rather than converted into an invented independent group count.

For `f01` and `f03`, disclose the reused source motifs and exact facts, but the observed overlap alone does not require rejecting their different task operations as contaminated. A conservative decision to retire the entire reserved bundle is available if the report needs a completely fresh set, but is stronger than the concrete evidence requires. The minimum warranted correction concerns `f02` and the blanket independence claim.

If the intended conclusion requires three groups wholly independent of calibration, replace the overlapping Russian group with an independently authored task whose source facts and answer template are not shared with the exposed probes. Fix that treatment independently of outcome scores. This review has not inspected those outcomes; if the coordinator has already received any, record that exposure rather than claiming the replacement decision preceded it. This is a measurement repair; it does not require changing F or repeating an unchanged failed answer. Without a replacement, report the narrower coverage honestly. Nothing in this finding supports an allegation that the executors received calibration keys, or that the selected method was changed after seeing final responses.
